description: The bar chart illustrates the percentage point difference in morphosyntactic probing performance between two multilingual BERT models — mBERT (light blue) and XLM-R (dark blue) — across three distinct model configurations: “hidden:[50], linear”, “hidden:[100], ReLU”, and “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU”. The vertical axis represents the “% point difference”, ranging from -0.2 to +0.2, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1, indicating how much one model outperforms or underperforms the other on a given configuration. For “hidden:[50], linear”, mBERT underperforms XLM-R by approximately 0.1 percentage point (mBERT ≈ -0.1, XLM-R ≈ 0.0). In “hidden:[100], ReLU”, mBERT underperforms by about 0.1 point (mBERT ≈ -0.12, XLM-R ≈ +0.03). For “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU”, mBERT underperforms by roughly 0.18 points (mBERT ≈ -0.18, XLM-R ≈ -0.13). The bars are grouped by configuration, with mBERT bars consistently positioned to the left of XLM-R bars within each group, and the legend in the upper right corner identifies the color coding. The chart suggests that XLM-R generally outperforms mBERT across all tested probing configurations, with the largest gap observed in the “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU” setup.
